name: OH-05
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+12 district with long-serving incumbent Bob Latta seeking re-election
Fundraising gap of roughly 125-to-1: Latta has $1.46M raised and $1.02M on hand vs. about $12K for Shaver
Prediction markets price Latta's win chance near 93 percent
No public polls or expert ratings; Libertarian nominee may trim the margin slightly
model.rationale: Latta holds a deeply Republican seat with a dominant money advantage and no outside spending against him, while his Democratic opponent is running a token campaign, and markets give the Democrat only about a 7 percent chance. With no polls or ratings suggesting competitive risk, the race sits firmly in Safe R territory.
model.watch: Only a major scandal or a historically lopsided national environment could narrow the margin meaningfully, and even then the seat would very likely stay Republican.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Northwest Ohio's fifth district leans about twelve points toward Republicans, and Bob Latta, first elected in 2007, is seeking another term. He has never faced a close general election here. His Democratic opponent, Brian Shaver, has raised roughly twelve thousand dollars, a tiny fraction of Latta's $1.5 million war chest, and no outside groups are active on either side. A Libertarian nominee also appears on the ballot.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the picture rests on fundamentals and market pricing. Prediction markets give Latta about a ninety-three percent chance of winning. The combination of district lean, incumbency, and the money gap points to a comfortable Republican victory, with the main uncertainty limited to the size of the margin.
